title: Anti-KID (Trompowsky, Torre & 4.Nf3)
intro: Answer the Trompowsky (2.Bg5) actively with 2...Ne4, meet the Torre (3.Bg5) with ...Bg7 and ...O-O, and handle 4.Nf3 cleanly.
variation: d2d4 g8f6 c1g5, d2d4 g8f6 g1f3 g7g6 c1g5, d2d4 g8f6 c2c4 g7g6 b1c3 f8g7 g1f3

lessons.title: The Trompowsky (2.Bg5)
lessons.summary: Jump to e4 against 2.Bg5 and strike the centre with ...d5 or ...c5.

steps.text: With 2.Bg5, White plays the Trompowsky Attack, threatening Bxf6 to double your pawns.
Step forward out of the pin and chase the bishop.
steps.hint: Jump to e4 with your f6 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...Ne4 to attack the g5 bishop and gain active piece play.
steps.ifRight: The bishop must declare where it is going.

steps.text: Claim central space and keep White's pieces out of e5.
steps.hint: Push the d-pawn two squares (or strike with ...c5).
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...d5 (or 3...c5) to fight for the centre right away.
steps.ifRight: After 3...d5 4.e3 c5, Black gets a comfortable, active game.

steps.text: If White tries 3.Bh4 to stay on the diagonal, strike at White's centre immediately.
steps.ifRight: 3...c5 gives Black great counterplay on the dark squares and c-file.

steps.text: After 3.Bf4 d5 4.e3, strike at White's centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...c5 to pressure d4 and open your queen to b6.
steps.ifRight: Black develops ...Nc6, ...Qb6 and ...Bf5 with a very healthy position.

steps.text: In the Torre Attack, White avoids c4 and pins the knight with 3.Bg5.

steps.hint: Put your f8 bishop on g7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Bg7 to protect the knight and eye the long diagonal.
steps.ifRight: Now Bxf6 leaves you with the bishop pair.

steps.text: Castle kingside before choosing your pawn break.
steps.ifRight: White usually sets up c3 and e3 or e4.

steps.text: White builds a solid pyramid with 5.c3.
Prepare ...e5 or ...c5 depending on White's next move.
steps.hint: Push the d-pawn one square to prepare ...Nbd7 and ...e5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...d6: after 6.e4, ...e5 (or ...Nbd7) gives Black strong central play.
steps.ifRight: Black plays ...Nbd7 and ...e5 (or ...c5) with a fine King's Indian.

lessons.title: When White Delays e4 (4.Nf3)
lessons.summary: Castle early, play ...d6 and ...Nbd7, and break with ...e5.

steps.text: White sometimes plays 4.Nf3 without e4 yet, keeping the option of e3, Bg5 or g3.
Castle kingside right away, keeping ...d6 and ...d5 both open.
Prepare ...Nbd7 and ...e5 against White's modest centre.
What if White pins your knight with 5.Bg5 before playing e3?
steps.hint: Play ...d6 to prepare ...Nbd7 and ...e5, or strike with ...c5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...d6 (or 5...c5): after 6.e3 Nbd7 7.Be2 e5, Black gets a smooth game.
steps.ifRight: Black prepares ...e5 or ...c5 with an easy position.

steps.text: White played 6.Be2. Continue your plan to push ...e5.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to d7 to support ...e5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Nbd7 (or 6...e5): after 6...Nbd7, ...e5 comes next with zero trouble.
steps.ifRight: Black pushes ...e5 next and gets lively central play.
